div.div:
Sprint 3 added two tables and three columns, in orange: the login lockout (FR57), the duplicate-scan alert (FR49), the transfer code a buyer claims with (FR40), and a company's private evidence of the craft and its consent to publish; plus a partial unique index that allows one open offer per product.
PK primary key · FK foreign key
1 exactly one · 0..1 at most one · * many

div.div:
Rules the database holds itself — a rule here survives a view that forgets it
Check constraints
company_track_matches_type a commercial company uses CHAMBER_OF_COMMERCE or OFFICIAL_REGISTRY; an artisan company uses ARTISAN_REVIEW
commercial_company_has_registry_code registry_code is filled for COMMERCIAL and empty for ARTISAN (FR08, FR09)
negative_decision_states_a_reason status_reason is filled when status is REJECTED or SUSPENDED (DBR12)
revocation_states_a_reason revocation_reason is filled when status is REVOKED (DBR12)
custody_transfer_changes_holder from_holder_id is not to_holder_id
Unique constraints — each chain of signed records stays linear
audit_entry_links_to_one_predecessor no audit entry is the predecessor of two others
custody_transfer_links_to_one_predecessor within one product, no handover is the predecessor of two others
custody_transfer_one_open_offer partial unique index on product_id WHERE state = INITIATED: one open offer per product, so a piece cannot be sold twice (FR35, Sprint 3)
alert_once_per_scan one alert per (product, scan) (FR49, Sprint 3)
accounts_loginattempt (email, ip_address) one failure streak per address and origin (FR57, Sprint 3)
